absent: Locking, lifetime and ownership rules for SST platform tables and pointed to arrays.
PM trace enable variable definition and generator output format and consumers.
Posted interrupt hardware delivery protocol for notification vector and destination beyond bit helpers.
Scheduler interaction and interrupt safety rules for preempt counter and reschedule flag.
Valid Cyrix register set and side effects of configuration accesses.
SME physical transforms and paging mode interactions for CR3 masks.
CPU topology discovery sources, update timing and synchronization.
TSS loading sequence, IO bitmap activation, fault handling and PKRU and shadow stack lifecycle.

findings.text: Audio stream routing uses a small record with six one byte members named dev_num, subdev_num, direction, device_id, task_id and status separating host device identity and substream position and transfer direction from firmware device and task identity plus liveness. Platform data carries this topology as a pointer named pdev_strm_map together with a count named strm_map_size.

Firmware memory description groups address bounds for instruction, data and isolated regions each paired with a use flag, plus a mailbox base, flags for ELF use and viewpoint requirement, and limits for stream count, DMA length and probe count. Members named iram_start, iram_end, iram_use, dram_start, dram_end, dram_use, imr_start, imr_end, imr_use, mailbox_start, use_elf, lpe_viewpt_rqd, max_streams, dma_max_len and num_probes convey placement and capacity.

Library download info records module base and end plus table offset and size and a flag for DDR download. Resource info records offsets and sizes for shim, serial port, DMA engines, memories and mailbox plus ACPI indices. IPC info records IPC and mailbox receive offsets. Platform info aggregates pointers named probe_data, ipc_info, res_info and lib_info with a platform name and a suspend loss flag named streams_lost_on_suspend.

Resume and suspend tracing share one contract. When a global enable is set, the call site line and file are captured into a dedicated tracedata section and forwarded with a caller supplied user value to a trace generator; when disabled they do nothing. Suspend is defined as an alias of resume.
Posted interrupt bit positions are zero for ON and one for SN, with table valid marker one. Request space spans two hundred fifty six vectors, with word count derived from vectors per machine word.

Posted descriptor holds a request bitmap named pir sized by word count, followed by a control union that can be viewed as separate notification count, vector, reserved byte and destination fields or as one sixty four bit control value, followed by six reserved words. The whole record is aligned to sixty four bytes.

Posted helpers expose atomic test and set or clear operations for ON, SN and individual PIR vector bits, plus plain set, clear and test for ON and SN, a PIR bit test, an emptiness check over the vector range, and a harvest operation. Harvest snapshots current request words, reports absence when all are clear, otherwise atomically clears only non empty words and returns collected values with presence indicated.
Two lightweight helpers directly set or clear the suppress bit inside the notification field without atomic primitives. MSI init for posted interrupts is provided as an empty inline with no effect.

Need reschedule marker occupies the most significant bit of an unsigned long, with enabled value combining zero count and that marker. Per CPU operation width has two build variants selecting sixty four bit or thirty two bit decrement spelling and matching eight or four byte raw CPU access.

Observed preempt count hides the need reschedule bit. Updating the count preserves that bit while replacing the remainder under a compare exchange retry. Initial task setup does nothing, while idle setup writes a disabled value into the per CPU counter for the target CPU.

Need reschedule state is active when its top bit is clear. Setting need clears the bit, clearing need sets it, and testing reports need when clear. Count helpers add or subtract through per CPU addition, with returning variants reporting the updated value, a decrement helper reporting whether the result reached zero, and a scheduler query reporting equality between the full counter including flag and a caller offset.

Dynamic preemption exposes enabled selectors bound to thunk symbols and disabled selectors as null, in both normal and notrace forms. The schedule entry has two build forms, one invoking a static call trampoline with module addressability and one calling the thunk directly, each mirrored for notrace.
Cyrix configuration access provides a byte read taking a register identifier and a byte write taking register and data, each delegating to underlying PC configuration get and set operations.

Virtual mode mask follows the flags VM bit when virtual eighty six is available and is zero otherwise. Address mask, PCID mask and no flush flag have a sixty four bit form using an SME cleared page mask, a twelve bit PCID field and the top bit, and a thirty two bit form using all ones low, zero PCID and zero no flush. PTI user PCID bit is eleven.

Network alignment is zero and hardware breakpoint count is four. Task and MM structure minimum alignments have one form scaling with internode cache shift and another using floating point state alignment for tasks and zero for MM structures.

Topology type enumerates any, performance, efficiency, low power and unknown. Topology record carries APIC and initial APIC ids, package, die, compute unit and core ids, logical mappings, AMD node id, cache domain ids, a hardware type union decoding Intel native model and type or AMD processor count, efficiency ranking, model and type, plus a vendor neutral Linux type.

CPU info groups vendor, family and model bytes sharing storage with a combined value, plus stepping, platform id, TLB size, VMX caps, virtual and physical bits, extended and maximum CPUID levels, an aligned capability array, vendor and model strings, topology and CPUID tables, cache size, alignment and QoS parameters, power, loops per jiffy, protection number, flush size, booted core count, CPU index, SMT state, microcode, cache address bits and an initialized flag under randomized layout.
Vendor identifiers run zero for Intel, one Cyrix, two AMD, three UMC, five Centaur, seven Transmeta, eight NSC, nine Hygon, ten Zhaoxin, eleven Vortex, with count twelve and unknown all ones byte.
Cache line size is read from boot CPU alignment. L1TF page frame limit is computed as a power of two from boot CPU cache address bits minus one minus page shift.

CR3 read returns the hardware value masked to address bits. Loading a page directory converts it through an SME physical transform then writes it. The write wrapper delegates to a native writer that moves the value into the control register with a memory barrier.

Thirty two bit hardware task state is a packed record of link, privilege stacks and segments, control register image, instruction pointer, flags, general registers, segment selectors, local descriptor selector, trace and bitmap base, reusing one segment slot to cache sysenter code selector. Sixty four bit form is a packed record of reserved fields, three privilege stacks with the third used as syscall scratch, seven interrupt stacks, further reserved words and bitmap base.

IO bitmap covers sixty five thousand five hundred thirty six bits, with byte and long counts derived from bit count. Valid offsets for map and full allow bitmaps are distances between task state fields. Kernel TSS limit has one form spanning bitmap plus trailing word and another spanning hardware state size. Invalid offset is one past the limit.

IO bitmap state pairs a previous sequence number and dirty size with two bitmaps sized one long beyond the nominal count, one general and one all allow for emulated privilege, where the trailing byte must remain set. Task state pairs hardware state with this bitmap state under page alignment. Entry stack is one page with page aligned wrapper, and IRQ stack is sized and aligned to its stack size.

Kernel GS base query returns the per CPU offset on symmetric builds and zero otherwise. Thread whitelist query delegates to floating point handling. Stack zero load writes the supplied value into the current CPU task state. GS swap issues the swap instruction only on sixty four bit builds.

Thread state holds TLS descriptors, stack pointers and segment selectors or bases differing by word size, an array of ptrace breakpoint slots sized by hardware count plus virtual status and user control values, fault address, trap number and error code, an optional virtual eighty six pointer, an IO bitmap pointer, emulated privilege level with a warn flag, a saved protection key value valid when descheduled, and optional shadow stack features when enabled.
Header include guards define unique macros for PM trace, posted interrupts, preemption, ROM probing, processor flags and processor headers to prevent repeated inclusion.

Posted state uses ON to mean a notification is outstanding and SN to suppress further notifications, with per vector request bits latched independently. Setting a PIR bit records work, harvest drains all set words, and ON and SN move between set and clear through atomic test and set or clear and plain set, clear and test operations, with direct non atomic updates reserved for contexts where races are already excluded.

Hardware task state must not cross a page boundary or errata may trigger. IO bitmap access reads one byte past the nominal end so that byte must exist, stay all ones and remain inside the limit. Request harvest must snapshot before clearing to avoid losing concurrent arrivals, relying on volatile reads and atomic exchange. Preempt counter updates must preserve the reschedule bit and use per CPU atomics.
